entry.title: 复数 (II)
entry.content:
复数 (II) (4) 复变函数 本章中，$k$ 表示任意整数． 4.1 复数的开方运算 一般地，如果复数 $w$ 满足 $wn=z(n\in\Bbb{N}*,z\in\Bbb{C})$，那么 $w$ 叫作 $z$ 的一个 $n$ 次方根，记作 $w=\sqrt[n]{z}$． 设 $z$ 和 $w$ 的三角形式为 $z=r(\cos\theta+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta),w=\rho(\cos\varphi+\mathrm{i}\sin\varphi)$，则根据棣莫弗公式有 $$ \begin{aligned} \big[\rho(\cos\varphi+\mathrm{i}\sin\varphi)\big]^n &= r(\cos\theta+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta) ~, \ \rho^n(\cos n\varphi+\mathrm{i}\sin n\varphi) &= r(\cos\theta+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta) ~. \end{aligned} $$ 则 $$ \begin{cases} \rho^n = r \implies \rho=\sqrt[n]{r} ~, \ n\varphi = \theta+2k\pi \implies \varphi=\frac{\theta}{n}+k\cdot\frac{2\pi}{n} ~. \end{cases} $$ 即 $$ w=\rho(\cos\varphi+\mathrm{i}\sin\varphi)=\sqrt[n]{r}\left[\cos\left(\frac{\theta}{n}+k\cdot\frac{2\pi}{n}\right)+\mathrm{i}\sin\left(\frac{\theta}{n}+k\cdot\frac{2\pi}{n}\right)\right] ~. $$ 由于 $\rho,r\in(\Bbb{R}_+\cup{0})$，故 $\rho$ 有唯一值． 容易发现，当 $k$ 取 $0,1,2,\dots,n-1$ 时，$w$ 有 $n$ 个不同的值． 再观察这 $n$ 个值的辐角，它们分别为 $\frac{\theta}{n},\frac{\theta}{n}+\frac{2\pi}{n},\dots,\frac{\theta}{n}+(n-1)\frac{2\pi}{n}$．容易发现，相邻两数的辐角都差 $\frac{2\pi}{n}$．又知它们的模都为 $\rho=\sqrt[n]{r}$，故这 $n$ 个数在复平面上平分以原点 $O$ 为圆心、半径为 $\rho=\sqrt[n]{r}$ 的圆周．
例 1：$\sqrt[3]{\mathrm{i}} = \left{\cos\frac{\pi}{6}+\mathrm{i}\sin\frac{\pi}{6},\cos\frac{5\pi}{6}+\mathrm{i}\sin\frac{5\pi}{6},\cos\frac{3\pi}{2}+\mathrm{i}\sin\frac{3\pi}{2}\right} = \left{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{i},-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{i},-\mathrm{i}\right}$． 这 $3$ 个解在复平面中的点如图 4-1 所示．
例 2：$\sqrt[5]{32} = \left{2,2\mathrm{e}{\mathrm{i}\frac{2\pi}{5}},2\mathrm{e}{\mathrm{i}\frac{4\pi}{5}},2\mathrm{e}{\mathrm{i}\frac{6\pi}{5}},2\mathrm{e}{\mathrm{i}\frac{8\pi}{5}}\right}$． 这 $5$ 个解在复平面中的点如图 4-2 所示．
4.2 复变函数的定义 代数基本定理 回顾上一节的内容．如果我们定义一个函数 $f(z)=\sqrt[n]{z}$（$n$ 是常数且 $n\in\Bbb{Z}$），容易发现，对于一个复数 $z$，$f(z)$ 不只有 $1$ 个值，而是有 $n$ 个值．这样的函数叫什么呢？ 一般地，设 $A$ 是一个复数集，$\forall z\in A$，通过一个确定的规则 $f$ 有一个或若干个复数 $w$ 与之对应，就说在复数集 $A$ 上定义了一个复变函数 (complex function)，记为 $w=f(z)$． 容易从定义中看到，一个复变函数 $w=f(z)$ 可能对于同一个数 $z$ 有多个值．其实实变函数中也有许多多值函数的例子，如 $\sin x$ 的反函数 $x=\sin y$（注意不是 $\arcsin x$），其定义域为 $[0,1]$，就是一个多值函数：
引入了复数的幂与根后，实数的多项式方程（一元 $n$ 次方程）可以被推广． 对于一元 $n$ 次方程 $a_nxn+a_{n-1}x{n-1}+a_{n-2}x{n-2}+\cdots+a_2x2+a_1x+a_0=0$，现在 $a$ 可以是复数了；其解 $x$ 也可以是复数了．同时，一些原来在实数域中无解的方程有了解． 如一元二次方程 $ax^2+bx+c=0 (a,b,c\in\Bbb{C})$，其两根为 $x=\dfrac{-b+\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}$，其中的平方根有两个值，故有两个解． 高斯 (Gauss) 1799 年第一次证明了代数基本定理 (Fundamental theorem of algebra)．其说明：任何一个一元复系数多项式方程都至少有一个复数根．或：任何一个非零的一元 $n$ 次复系数多项式，都正好有 $n$ 个复数根（重根视为多个根）.
该定理的证明较为困难．但是，我们可以从复数的开方运算中获得一个直观的认识． 4.3 复变指数函数 4.3.1 实变指数函数 欧拉指出的指数函数 $\exp x$ 定义： $$ \exp x = \lim_{n\to\infty}\left(1+\frac{x}{n}\right)^n $$ 由于有 $\mathrm{e}=\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\left(1+\frac{1}{n}\right)n,\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\left(\left(1+\frac{1}{n}\right)n\right)^x=\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\left(1+\frac{x}{n}\right)$，故 $$ \mathrm{e}^x = \exp x ~. $$ 实变指数函数具有以下性质：
$\left(\mathrm{e}x\right)'=\mathrm{e}x$，即 $\exp’x=\exp x$，其处处可导； $ax=\mathrm{e}{x\ln a}$； $\mathrm{e}{x+y}=\mathrm{e}x\mathrm{e}^y$，即 $\exp(x+y)=\exp x\exp y$； $\mathrm{e}{xy}=\left(\mathrm{e}x\right)^y$；即 $\exp xy=\exp^y x$； $\mathrm{e}{-x}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}x}$，即 $\exp(-x)=\frac{1}{\exp x}$．
它们对任意 $x,y\in\Bbb{R}$ 都是有效的． 4.3.2 复变指数函数 我们试图把 $\exp x$ 推广到复数域． 设此函数为 $f(z)$．我们希望它与实变的指数函数 $\exp x$ 具有相似的性质．具体来说：
$f(z)$ 处处可导； $f’(z)=f(z)$； $f(x_0)=\mathrm{e}^{x_0}$
这个函数存在且唯一．我们将其称为复变指数函数 (complex exponential function)，记作 $\exp (x+\mathrm{i}y)~(x,y\in\Bbb{R})$．有 $$ \exp (x+\mathrm{i}y)=\mathrm{e}^x(\cos y+\mathrm{i}\sin y)=\mathrm{e}x\mathrm{e}{\mathrm{i}y} ~. $$ 验证，可知其满足上述条件．（我也不会，反正是对的） 对于指数函数，有重要等式 $\mathrm{e}a\mathrm{e}b=\mathrm{e}^{a+b}$． 验证可得： $$ \exp z_1\cdot\exp z_2 = \mathrm{e}{x_1}\mathrm{e}{\mathrm{i}y_1}\mathrm{e}{x_2}\mathrm{e}{\mathrm{i}y_2}=\mathrm{e}{x_1+x_2}\mathrm{e}{\mathrm{i}(y_1+y_2)}=\exp(z_1+z_2) $$ 可以发现，这个函数的性质与实变指数函数的性质几乎一模一样．那么，在不引起歧义的情况下，我们就用 $\mathrm{e}^z$ 来表示 $\exp z$，即： $$ \mathrm{e}^z = \exp z ~. $$ 要注意此处 $\mathrm{e}^z$ 只是代替 $\exp z$ 的一种写法，不能理解为 $\mathrm{e}$ 的 $z$ 次幂．这是两个不同的概念． 令 $x=0$，即得欧拉公式 $\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\theta} = (\cos\theta+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta)$．
例：$\mathrm{e}^{2+\mathrm{i}} = \mathrm{e}2\mathrm{e}{\mathrm{i}}$．这是一个模为 $\mathrm{e}^2$，辐角为 $1 ~\text{rad}$ 的数．
4.4 复变对数函数 复变对数函数定义为指数函数的反函数． 即，如果 $\mathrm{e}^w=z$，那么 $w$ 关于 $z$ 的函数就是复变对数函数 (complex logarithm function)，记作 $w=\operatorname{Ln}z$． 已知 $z=r\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\theta}$，我们来求一下 $w$． 设 $w=a+b\mathrm{i}$，则有 $$ \begin{aligned} \mathrm{e}^{a+b\mathrm{i}} &= r\mathrm{e}^{i\theta} ~, \ \mathrm{e}a\mathrm{e}{b\mathrm{i}} &= r\mathrm{e}^{i\theta} ~. \end{aligned} $$ 则 $$ \begin{cases} \mathrm{e}^a=r \iff a=\ln r ~, \ b=\theta+2k\pi ~. \end{cases} $$ 故 $w=\operatorname{Ln}z=\ln r+(\theta+2k\pi)\mathrm{i}$． 容易发现，对数函数 $w=\operatorname{Ln}z$ 也是一个多值函数，它的所有值在与实轴垂直的一条直线上． 若 $\theta+2k\pi=\theta_0=\arg z$，那么此时 $w$ 的值称为 $z$ 对数的主值 (principal value)，记作 $\ln z$，有 $\ln z = \ln r+\theta_0\mathrm{i}$．容易发现，$\operatorname{Ln}z=\ln z+2k\pi\mathrm{i}$． 对于一个固定的 $k$，$\operatorname{Ln}z$ 会变成一个单值函数，这时的 $\operatorname{Ln}z$ 称为其的一个分支 (branch)．主值也是它的一个分支 . 复变对数函数满足实变对数函数的某些性质．如：
$\operatorname{Ln}(xy)=\operatorname{Ln}x+\operatorname{Ln}y$； $\operatorname{Ln}\left(\vcenter{\frac{x}{y}}\right)=\operatorname{Ln}x-\operatorname{Ln}y$ .
但同时，某些性质不满足．如：
$\operatorname{Ln}(x^n)\neq n\operatorname{Ln}x$（$n$ 是大于 $1$ 的正整数）
下面证明 $\operatorname{Ln}(x^n)\neq n\operatorname{Ln}x$：
证明：
下面举几个例子：
$\operatorname{Ln}(-1)=\ln 1+(\pi+2k\pi)\mathrm{i}=(2k+1)\pi\mathrm{i}$ $\operatorname{Ln}(1+\mathrm{i})=\ln\sqrt{2}+\left(\vcenter{\frac{\pi}{4}}+2k\pi\right)\mathrm{i}=\frac{\ln 2}{2}+\left(\vcenter{\frac{\pi}{4}}+2k\pi\right)\mathrm{i}$
4.5 复数的复数次幂 有了复数的指数函数和对数函数，我们就可以定义复数的乘幂了 . 如果 $a,b\in\Bbb{C}$，那么我们定义 $ab=\mathrm{e}{b\operatorname{Ln}a}=\exp(b\operatorname{Ln}a)$．注意到这里的 $\mathrm{e}^z$ 为指数函数 $\exp z$ . $\operatorname{Ln}a$ 是多值的，$b\operatorname{Ln}a$ 就是多值的，所以整体也就是多值的 . 到这就可以理解为什么 $\mathrm{e}^z$ 理解为指数函数和幂是不一样的了．举个例子：
$\exp\mathrm{i} = \cos 1+\mathrm{i}\sin 1$； $\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}} = \exp(i\operatorname{Ln}\mathrm{e}) = \exp\big[\mathrm{i}(\ln\mathrm{e}+2k\pi\mathrm{i})\big] = \exp(\mathrm{i}+2k\pi) = (\cos 1+\sin 1)e^{2k\pi}$． 显然这两个式子的值完全不同 .
事实上，在这种乘幂的定义下，只要底数 $a\neq 0$：
指数 $b\in\Bbb{Z}$ 时，$a^b$ 单值； 指数 $b\in\Bbb{Q}$ 时，若 $b=\frac{p}{q} (p,q\in\Bbb{Z},\gcd(p,q)=1)$，$a^b$ 有 $q$ 个值； 指数 $b$ 为其他数（无理数或虚数）时，$a^b$ 有无穷多个值． 比如 $1\pi,(1+\mathrm{i}){\sqrt[3]{2}},\mathrm{i}\mathrm{i},(2+\mathrm{i}){1+2\mathrm{i}}$ 都有无穷多个值． 其中有趣的是，计算可得 $\mathrm{i}^\mathrm{i} = \exp(\mathrm{i}\operatorname{Ln}\mathrm{i}) = \exp\left[\mathrm{i}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi\right)\mathrm{i}\right]=\exp\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi\right)\in\Bbb{R}$ .
下面逐个证明上面三条 .
设 $a=r\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\theta}$ .
(1) 指数 $b\in\Bbb{Z}$ 时，$a^b$ 单值 .
证明：当 $b\in\Bbb{Z}$ 时，有： $$ \begin{aligned} a^b &= \exp(b\operatorname{Ln}a) \ &= \exp\left(b\left(\ln r+\left(\theta+2k\pi\right)\mathrm{i}\right)\right) \ &= \exp(b\ln r+b(\theta+2k\pi)\mathrm{i}) \ &= \mathrm{e}^{b\ln r}\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}(b\theta+b\cdot 2k\pi)} \ \because b\in\Bbb{Z},\therefore a^b &= \mathrm{e}^{b\ln r}\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}b\theta} \end{aligned} $$ 结果唯一．证毕 .
(2) 指数 $b\in\Bbb{Q}$ 时，若 $b=\frac{p}{q} (p,q\in\Bbb{Z},\gcd(p,q)=1)$，$a^b$ 有 $q$ 个值．
证明：当 $b=\frac{p}{q}\in\Bbb{Q}~(p,q\in\Bbb{Z},\gcd(p,q)=1)$ 时，有 $$ \begin{aligned} a^b &= \exp(b\operatorname{Ln}a) \ &= \exp\left(\vcenter{\frac{p}{q}\left(\ln r+\left(\theta+2k\pi\right)\right)}\right) \ &= \exp\left(\vcenter{\frac{p\ln r+p\left(\theta+2k\pi\right)\mathrm{i}}{q}}\right) \ &= \exp\left(\vcenter{\frac{p\ln r}{q}+\frac{p\left(\theta+2k\pi\right)\mathrm{i}}{q}}\right) \ &= \mathrm{e}^{\frac{p\ln r}{q}}\cdot\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\left(\vcenter{\frac{p}{q}\theta+pk\cdot\frac{2\pi}{q}}\right)} \end{aligned} $$ $\mathrm{e}^{\frac{p\ln r}{q}}$ 是实数域内的计算，值唯一；$\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\left(\frac{p}{q}\theta+pk\cdot\frac{2\pi}{q}\right)}$ 中，由于 $\gcd(p,q)=1$，故有 $q$ 个不同值．故该式整体上有 $q$ 个不同值．证毕．
(3) 指数 $b$ 为其他数（无理数或虚数）时，$a^b$ 有无穷多个值．
证明略．显而易见．
4.6 复变三角函数与双曲函数 to do.

entry.title: 复数 (I)
entry.content:
复数 (I) (0) 数集的扩充 自人类诞生以来，数的概念就在不断地发展着． 为了计数的需要，人们发展了自然数集的概念，建立了自然数集 $\Bbb{N}$． 在自然数集 $\Bbb{N}$ 中，加法与乘法总能实施．但是，小数不能减大数，方程 $x+6=0$ 无解．由此引入负数，数集扩展到整数集 $\Bbb{Z}$． 在整数集 $\Bbb{Z}$ 中，加法、减法与乘法总能实施．但是，由于除法只能解决整除的问题，方程 $3x-2=0$ 无解．由此引入分数，数集扩展到有理数集 $\Bbb{Q}$． 在有理数集 $\Bbb{Q}$ 中，加法、减法、乘法与除法（除数不为 $0$）总能实施．但是，开方的结果可能不是有理数，方程 $x^2-2=0$ 无解．由此引入无理数，数集扩展到实数集 $\Bbb{R}$． 在实数集 $\Bbb{R}$ 中，加法、减法、乘法与除法（除数不为 $0$）总能实施，并解决了正数的开方问题． 现在在实数集 $\Bbb{R}$ 中，我们又面临着方程 $x^2+1=0$ 无解，负数不能开平方的问题．这表明，数的概念仍需要进一步发展． (1) 定义 为了使得方程 $x^2+1=0$ 有解，使实数的开方运算总能实施，我们引入一个新数 $\mathrm{i}$，叫做虚数单位 (imaginary unit)，并规定：
$\mathrm{i}^2=-1$； 实数可与 $\mathrm{i}$ 进行四则运算，且原有的加法、乘法运算律仍成立．
从而，$\mathrm{i}$ 可与实数 $b$ 相乘，再与实数 $a$ 相加，得到一个数 $a+b\mathrm{i}$． 这样，数的范围又扩充了，出现了形如 $a+b\mathrm{i}(a,b\in\Bbb{R})$ 的数，这种树叫做复数 (complex number)，全体复数组成的集合叫做复数集 (set of complex numbers)，记作 $\Bbb{C}$．显然有 $\Bbb{N}\subseteq\Bbb{Z}\subseteq\Bbb{Q}\subseteq\Bbb{R}\subseteq\Bbb{C}$． 复数通常用字母 $z$ 表示，即 $z=a+b\mathrm{i}(a,b\in\Bbb{R})$，其中 $a$ 和 $b$ 分别叫做复数 $z$ 的实部 (real part) 和虚部 (imaginary part)，记作 $\operatorname{Re}z,\Re z,\mathfrak{R} z$ 与 $\operatorname{Im}z,\Im z,\mathfrak{I} z$．其中，国标要求为 $\operatorname{Re}z$ 与 $\operatorname{Im}z$．下文为简便，使用 $\Re z$ 与 $\Im z$． 当且仅当 $b=\Im z=0$ 时，$z\in \Bbb{R}$．当 $b=\Im z\neq 0$ 时，$z$ 叫作虚数 (imaginary number)． 特别地，当 $a=\Re z=0$ 且 $b=\Im z\neq 0$ 时，$z$ 叫作纯虚数 (pure imaginary number)． 即 $$ \text{复数} ~ z=a+b\mathrm{i} \begin{cases} \text{实数} & (b=0),\ \text{虚数} & (b\neq 0)(\text{当}a=0~\text{时为纯虚数}) ~. \end{cases} $$ 如果两个复数的实部与虚部分别相等，那么我们就说这两个复数相等，即 $$ z_1=z_2 \iff \Re z_1=\Re z_2 \text{且} \Im z_1=\Im z_2 ~. $$ 或 $$ a+b\mathrm{i}=c+d\mathrm{i} \iff a=c \text{且} b=d ~. $$ 也就是说
两个复数相等的充要条件是它们的实部和虚部分别相等．
(2) 复数的运算 本节中，$a,b,c,d\in\Bbb{R}$． 已经知道虚数单位 $\mathrm{i}$ 与实数一起可以按照实数的运算法则进行运算． 2.1 复数的加减 相反数 设 $z_1=a+b\mathrm{i},z_2=c+d\mathrm{i}$，复数的加法如此计算： $$ (a+b\mathrm{i})+(c+d\mathrm{i})=(a+c)+(b+d)\mathrm{i} ~. $$ 显然，两个复数的和仍为复数． 容易验证，复数的加法满足交换律与结合律，即 $\forall z_1,z_2,z_3\in\Bbb{C}$，有 $$ \begin{aligned} z_1+z_2 & = z_2+z_1 ~,\ (z_1+z_2)+z_3 & = z_1+(z_2+z_3) ~. \end{aligned} $$ 我们将满足 $(c+d\mathrm{i})+(x+y\mathrm{i})=a+b\mathrm{i}$ 的复数 $x+y\mathrm{i} (x,y\in\Bbb{R})$ 叫作复数 $a+b\mathrm{i}$ 减去复数 $c+d\mathrm{i}$ 所得的差，记作 $$ (a+b\mathrm{i})-(c+d\mathrm{i}) ~. $$ 明显有 $$ c+x=a,d+y=b , $$ 即 $$ x=a-c,y=b-d , $$ 所以 $$ x+y\mathrm{i}=(a-c)+(b-d)\mathrm{i} ~. $$ 于是得到复数的减法法则： $$ (a+b\mathrm{i})-(c+d\mathrm{i})=(a-c)+(b-d)\mathrm{i} ~. $$ 类似于实数，定义复数 $z=a+b\mathrm{i}$ 的相反数 $-z=-a-b\mathrm{i}$． 那么复数的减法法则也可以是：$(z_1,z_2\in\Bbb{C})$ $$ z_1-z_2=z_1+(-z_2) ~. $$ 2.2 复数的乘法与正整数次幂 复数的乘法这样计算： $$ (a+b\mathrm{i})(c+d\mathrm{i})=ac+ad\mathrm{i}+bc\mathrm{i}+bd\mathrm{i}^2 , $$ 即 $$ (a+b\mathrm{i})(c+d\mathrm{i})=(ac-bd)+(bc+ad)\mathrm{i} ~. $$ 显然，两个复数的积仍为复数． 容易验证，复数的乘法满足交换律、结合律以及分配律，即 $\forall z_1,z_2,z_3\in\Bbb{C}$，有 $$ \begin{aligned} z_1z_2 & = z_2z_1 ~,\ (z_1z_2)z_3 & = z_1(z_2z_3) ~,\ z_1(z_2+z_3) & = z_1z_2+z_1z_3 ~. \end{aligned} $$ 复数的乘方是相同复数的积．根据复数乘法运算律，实数内正整数指数幂的运算律在复数范围内仍成立，即对于任何 $z,z_1,z_2\in\Bbb{C},m,n\in\Bbb{N}^*$，有 $$ \begin{aligned} zmzn & = z^{m+n} ~,\ (zm)n & = z^{mn} ~,\ (z_1z_2)^n & = z_1nz_2n ~. \end{aligned} $$ 计算复数乘方时，需用到虚数单位 $\mathrm{i}$ 的乘方： $$ \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{i}1=\mathrm{i},\mathrm{i}2=-1,\mathrm{i}3=-\mathrm{i},\mathrm{i}4=1\ \implies & \mathrm{i}{4n}=1,\mathrm{i}{4n+1}=\mathrm{i},\mathrm{i}{4n+2}=-1,\mathrm{i}{4n+3}=-\mathrm{i} ~. \end{aligned} $$ 2.3 共轭复数与复数的除法 我们把实部相等，虚部互为相反数的两个复数叫作互为共轭复数 (complex conjugate)．复数 $z=a+b\mathrm{i}$ 的共轭复数记作 $\bar z$ 或 $\operatorname{conj}z$，即 $$ \bar z = \operatorname{conj} z = a-b\mathrm{i} $$ 当 $b=0$ 时，$z=\bar z$．也就是说，实数的共轭数是它本身． 容易发现 $$ z\bar z = (a+b\mathrm{i})(a-b\mathrm{i})=a2-b2\mathrm{i}2=a2+b^2 ~. $$ 我们把满足 $$ (c+d\mathrm{i})(x+y\mathrm{i})=a+b\mathrm{i} ~ (c+d\mathrm{i}\neq 0) $$ 的复数 $x+y\mathrm{i}(x,y\in\Bbb{R})$ 叫作复数 $a+b\mathrm{i}$ 除以 $c+d\mathrm{i}$ 所得的商，记作 $\dfrac{a+b\mathrm{i}}{c+d\mathrm{i}}$ 或 $(a+b\mathrm{i})\div(c+d\mathrm{i})$． 容易证明，$\dfrac{z_1}{z_2}=\dfrac{z_1z}{z_2z}(z,z_1,z_2\in\Bbb{C}\text{且}z,z_2\neq0)$． 一般地，我们有 $$ \frac{a+b\mathrm{i}}{c+d\mathrm{i}} = \frac{(a+b\mathrm{i})(c-d\mathrm{i})}{(c+d\mathrm{i})(c-d\mathrm{i})} = \frac{ac+bd}{c2+d2}+\frac{bc-ad}{c2+d2}\mathrm{i} ~. $$ 因为 $c+d\mathrm{i}\neq 0$，所以 $c2+d2\neq 0$． 由此可见，两个复数的商仍为复数． 由此也就可以定义复数 $z$ 的倒数 $\frac{1}{z}$． 2.4 复数的整数次幂 类似于实数，复数 $z$ 的负整数幂 $z{-m}(m\in\Bbb{N}*)$ 定义为对应正整数幂的倒数，即 $$ z{-m}=\frac{1}{zm} ~. $$ 并且有 $z^0=1(z\neq 0)$．复数乘方满足实数乘方所有运算律． (3) 复数的几何意义 3.1 复平面 模与辐角 对于每一个复数 $z=a+b\mathrm{i} (a,b\in\Bbb{R})$，都有唯一的数对 $(a,b)$ 与其对应．同时，在直角坐标系中的每一个点，也都有唯一确定的数对 $(a,b)$ 与其对应． 因此，我们可以仿照直角坐标系，建立一个平面，将复数 $z=a+b\mathrm{i}$ 与平面上的点一一对应．
如图 3-1．这个平面叫作复平面 (complex plane) 或阿甘得图 (Argand diagram)，$x$ 轴叫作实轴 (real axis)，$y$ 轴叫作虚轴 (imaginary axis)．显然，实轴上的点都表示实数；除原点外，虚轴上的点都表示虚数．容易发现，复平面实质上是数轴的扩展． 可以发现，复数 $z=a+b\mathrm{i}$ 同时与向量 $\overrightarrow{OZ}$ 一一对应，于是，我们也可以用一个向量 $\overrightarrow{OZ}$ 来表示复数． 在此基础上，我们把向量 $\overrightarrow{OZ}$ 的模（即 $Z$ 到 $O$ 的距离）$r$ 称为复数 $z$ 的模 (module) 或强度 (magnitude) 或绝对值 (absolute value)，用 $\lvert z\rvert$ 表示．图 3-1 中 $r$ 即为 $z$ 的模．容易得到， $\lvert z\rvert=\sqrt{a2+b2}$，$\lvert z\rvert\in\Bbb{R}$ 且 $\lvert z\rvert\ge 0$． 我们把实轴正半轴旋转到向量 $\overrightarrow{OZ}$ 方向的角 $\theta$（或 $\varphi$）称为复数 $z$ 的辐角 (argument)或相位 (phase)，记作 $\operatorname{Arg} z$．容易发现，一个复数 $z$ 的辐角有无穷多个，因此，我们将处在区间 $[0,2\pi)$（更常用的另一种区间为 $(-\pi,\pi]$）的辐角称为复数 $z$ 的辐角主值 (principal value of argument)，记作 $\arg z$． 显然，每一个非零复数 $z=a+b\mathrm{i}$ 都有唯一确定的模和辐角主值；反过来，复数模和辐角主值可以唯一确定这个复数．于是
两个非零复数相等的充要条件是这两个复数的模与辐角主值分别相等．
即 $$ z_1=z_2 \iff \lvert z_1\rvert=\lvert z_2\rvert \text{且} \arg z_1=\arg z_2 ~(z_1,z_2\neq 0) ~. $$ 复数 $z=0$ 与原点 $O(0,0)$ 对应，向量 $\overrightarrow{OZ}=\mathbf{0}$，此时复数的模为 $0$，辐角是任意的．有时为了方便讨论，会规定 $z=0$ 的辐角主值为 $0$． 3.2 复数加减法的几何意义 如图 3-2，向量 $\overrightarrow{OZ_1},\overrightarrow{OZ_2}$ 分别与复数 $a+b\mathrm{i},c+d\mathrm{i}$ 对应，且 $\overrightarrow{OZ_1},\overrightarrow{OZ_2}$ 不共线，以 $\overrightarrow{OZ_1},\overrightarrow{OZ_2}$ 为两条邻边画平行四边形，则对角线 $OZ$ 所表示的向量 $\overrightarrow{OZ}$ 就是与复数 $(a+c)+(b+d)\mathrm{i}$ 对应的向量．这就是复数加法的几何意义．
根据复数减法的定义以及复数加法的几何意义，可以得到复数减法的几何意义． 如图 3-3，，若向量 $\overrightarrow{OZ_1},\overrightarrow{OZ_2}$ 分别与复数 $z_1,z_2$ 对应，则它们的差 $z_1-z_2$ 对应着 向量 $\overrightarrow{OZ_1}-\overrightarrow{OZ_2}$，即向量 $\overrightarrow{Z_2Z_1}$． 如果作 $\overrightarrow{OZ}=\overrightarrow{Z_2Z_1}$，那么点 $Z$ 对应的复数就是 $z_1-z_2$．这就是复数减法的几何意义．
设 $z_1=a+b\mathrm{i},z_2=c+d\mathrm{i}$，则 $z_1-z_2=(a-c)+(b-d)\mathrm{i}$，故 $$ \lvert z_1-z_2 \rvert = \left\lvert \overrightarrow{OZ} \right\rvert = \left\lvert \overrightarrow{Z_2Z_1} \right\rvert = \sqrt{(a-c)2+(b-d)2} ~. $$ 这表明：两个复数的差的模就是复平面内与这两个复数对应的两点间的距离． 3.3 复数的三角形式 由图 3-1 易得（$r=\lvert z\rvert,\theta=\operatorname{Arg} z$） $$ a=r\cos\theta,b=r\sin\theta ~. $$ 于是，可以得到 $z=a+b\mathrm{i}=r\cos\theta+\mathrm{i}r\sin\theta=r(\cos\theta+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta)$．这就是复数 $z$ 的三角形式 (trigonometric form of complex numbers)，而 $a+b\mathrm{i}$ 称为复数 $z$ 的代数形式 (algebraic form of complex numbers)． 有时，会使用 $\operatorname{cis}\theta$ 代替 $\cos\theta+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta$． 3.4 复数乘除法的几何意义 棣莫弗公式 设复数 $z_1=r_1(\cos\theta_1+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta_1),z_2=r_2(\cos\theta_2+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta_2)$．若它们的乘积为 $z=z_1z_2$，且 $z=r(\cos\theta+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta)$，则根据三角函数和角公式有 $$ \begin{aligned} z=z_1z_2 &= r_1(\cos\theta_1+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta_1)\cdot r_2(\cos\theta_2+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta_2) \ &= r_1r_2(\cos\theta_1\cos\theta_2+\mathrm{i}\cos\theta_1\sin\theta_2+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta_1\cos\theta_2+\mathrm{i}^2\sin\theta_1\sin\theta_2) \ &= r_1r_2\big[(\cos\theta_1\cos\theta_2-\sin\theta_1\sin\theta_2)+\mathrm{i}(\sin\theta_1\cos\theta_2+\cos\theta_1\sin\theta_2)\big] \ &= r_1r_2\big[\cos(\theta_1+\theta_2)+\mathrm{i}\sin(\theta_1+\theta_2)\big] \ \end{aligned} $$ 上式称为棣莫弗公式 (De Moivre’s formula) 或棣莫弗定理．于是可以得到 $$ r=r_1r_2,\theta=\theta_1+\theta_2 ~. $$ 即：
两个复数相乘，其积的模等于这两个复数的模的积，其积的辐角等于这两个复数的辐角的和．
由此可得出复数乘法的几何意义． 类似的，可以得出复数除法的几何意义． 根据棣莫弗公式，设有 $n$ 个复数 $z_1=r_1(\cos\theta_1+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta_1),z_2=r_2(\cos\theta_2+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta_2),\cdots,z_n=r_n(\cos\theta_n+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta_n)$，则有： $$ z_1z_2\cdots z_n = r_1r_2\cdots r_n\big[\cos(\theta_1+\theta_2+\cdots+\theta_n)+\mathrm{i}\sin(\theta_1+\theta_2+\cdots+\theta_n)\big] ~. $$ 即： $$ \prod_{i=1}^{n}z_i = \prod_{i=1}{n}r_i\cdot\left(\cos\sum_{i=1}{n}\theta_i+\mathrm{i}\sin\sum_{i=1}^{n}\theta_i\right) ~. $$ 这称为一般的棣莫弗公式． 若令 $z_1=z_2=\cdots=z_n=z=r(\cos\theta+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta)$，则有 $$ z^n = \big[r(\cos\theta+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta)\big]^n = r^n(\cos n\theta+\mathrm{i}\sin n\theta) ~. $$ 即为复数的乘方公式．其为棣莫弗公式的一个特例． 3.5 欧拉公式 复数的指数形式
欧拉 (Euler) 对复数进行了系统研究后，得出欧拉公式 (Euler’s formula)： $$ \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\theta} = \cos\theta+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta ~. $$ 当 $\theta=\pi$ 时，即为著名的欧拉恒等式： $$ \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\pi} = -1 ~. $$ 欧拉证明此公式时，使用了此方法（方法一），而促进了复数域指数函数（$\exp z$ 等）的产生．但由于复数域中的泰勒展开等运算均需用到欧拉公式，故此一方法会造成循环论证，而不能作为证明，只能作为一种“验证方法”． 下面证明过程引自 Wikipedia：
首先，在复数域上对 $\mathrm{e}^x$ 进行定义：
对于 $a,b\in\Bbb{R},c=a+b\mathrm{i}\in\Bbb{C}$，规定 $\mathrm{e}c=\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\left(1+\dfrac{c}{n}\right)n$．
对复数的三角形式 $w=u+v\mathrm{i}=r(\cos\theta+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta)$，有： $$ r=\sqrt{u2+v2}\in\Bbb{R},\theta=\arctan\left(\frac{v}{u}\right)\in\Bbb{R} ~. $$ 且根据棣莫弗公式，$wn=(u+v\mathrm{i})n=r^n(\cos n\theta+\mathrm{i}\sin n\theta)$． 从而有： $$ \left(1+\frac{a+b\mathrm{i}}{n}\right) = \left[\left(1+\frac{a}{n}\right)+\mathrm{i}\cdot\frac{b}{n}\right] = rn(\cos\thetan+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta^n) ~. $$ 假设 $n>\lvert a\rvert$，则： $$ rn=\left[\left(1+\frac{a}{n}\right)+\left(\frac{b}{n}\right)2\right]{\frac{n}{2}},\thetan=n\arctan\frac{\frac{b}{n}}{1+\frac{a}{n}} ~. $$ 为除去幂上的 $n$，两边取对数得 $$ \begin{aligned} \lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\ln r^n &= \lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\left[\frac{n}{2}\ln\left(1+\frac{2a}{n}+\frac{a2+b2}{n^2}\right)\right] \ &= \lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\left[\frac{n}{2}\left(\frac{2a}{n}+\frac{a2+b2}{n^2}\right)\right] \ &= a ~. \end{aligned} $$ 这一步骤用到 $\ln(1+x)\approx x$（墨卡托级数）. 即： $$ \lim\limits_{n\to\infty}r^n = \lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\mathrm{e}^{\ln r^n} = \mathrm{e}^a ~. $$ 又有（$\arctan x$ 在 $0$ 附近约等于 $0$）： $$ \begin{aligned} \lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\theta^n &= \lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\left(n\arctan\frac{\frac{b}{n}}{1+\frac{a}{n}}\right) \ &= \lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\left(n\cdot\frac{\frac{b}{n}}{1+\frac{a}{n}}\right) \ &= b ~. \end{aligned} $$ 从而可以证明： $$ \lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\left(1+\frac{a+b\mathrm{i}}{n}\right)^n = \mathrm{e}^a(\cos b+\mathrm{i}\sin b) ~. $$ 即： $$ \mathrm{e}^{a+\mathrm{i}b} = \mathrm{e}^a(\cos b+\mathrm{i}\sin b) ~. $$ 令 $a=0$，可得欧拉公式． 证毕．
利用欧拉公式与复数的三角形式，可以得到： $$ z=a+b\mathrm{i}=r(\cos\theta+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta)=r\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\theta} ~. $$ $z=r\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\theta}$ 称为复数 $z$ 的指数形式 (exponential form of complex numbers)． 复数的三角形式与指数形式由于都用模 $r$ 与辐角 $\theta$ 表示复数，故又称为复数的极坐标形式 (polar form of complex numbers)；同样的，复数的代数形式又称为复数的直角坐标形式 (cartesian form of complex numbers)．

entry.title: 洛谷 P1131 题解
entry.content:
传送门 题意 有一棵 $n$ 个节点的以 $s$ 为根的树。每条树边都有一个长度。每次操作可以把一条树边的长度加 $1$。 问：至少操作多少次，可以使根节点到每个叶子节点的距离相等。 结论 $1$ 对于任意子树，其根节点到其每个叶子节点的距离相等。
证明： 反证法。 设对于根为 $R$ 的树的根为 $r$ 的某一子树，有两个叶子 $a$、$b$ 到 $r$ 的距离不等。 那么不妨设节点 $x$ 与 $y$ 间的距离为 $dis(x,y)$，则有 $$dis(a,r)\not=dis(b,r)$$ 所以 $$dis(a,r)+dis(r,R)\not=dis(b,r)+dis(r,R)$$ 得 $$dis(a,R)\not=dis(b,R)$$ 即 $a$、$b$ 到 $R$ 的距离不等。这与题目条件矛盾，所以命题成立。
解法 既然结论 $1$ 成立，那么先从最简单的情况入手。 如图，在这一棵以 $1$ 为根的树中，在操作后，根节点 $1$ 到叶子的距离最小是几？
很明显的，这个值应该是所有叶子到根的所有距离的最大值。 那么对于每个节点都实行此原则，就结束了。 Code： #include <bits/stdc++.h>using namespace std;using uint = unsigned;using ll = long long;using ull = unsigned long long;using pii = pair<int,int>;using pll = pair<ll,ll>;#define int llint hd[500005<<1],nxt[500005<<1],to[500005<<1],we[500005<<1],et=0;inline void adde(int u,int v,int w) { ++et,to[et]=v,we[et]=w,nxt[et]=hd[u],hd[u]=et; }int n,s,ans,dp[500005];void dfs(int u,int fa) { int mx=0,tot=0; for(int i=hd[u],v,t; v=to[i],t=we[i],i; i=nxt[i]) { if(v==fa) continue; dfs(v,u); if(dp[v]+t>mx) { ans+=(dp[v]+t-mx)*tot; mx=dp[v]+t; } else ans+=(mx-dp[v]-t); ++tot; } dp[u]=mx;}signed main() { cin>>n>>s; for(int i=1; i<n; ++i) { int u,v,t; cin>>u>>v>>t; adde(u,v,t); adde(v,u,t); } dfs(s,0); cout<<ans<<endl;}

entry.title: 中线定理的几种证明
entry.content:
中线定理 如图，在 $\triangle ABC$ 中，$D$ 是 $BC$ 的中点，则有 $$ AB2+AC2 = 2AD2+\frac{1}{2}BC2 = 2AD2+2BD2 = 2AD2+2CD2 ~. $$ 即三角形一条中线两侧所对的边平方和等于底边平方的一半与该边中线平方的两倍的和 .
以下讨论中，设 $AD=x,AB=c,AC=b,BC=a$，原命题即化为 $$ b2+c2 = 2x2+\frac{1}{2}a2 ~. $$ 第 1 种（繁）
如图，在 $\triangle ABC$ 中，有 $\overrightarrow{AD}=\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BD}=\overrightarrow{AC}+\overrightarrow{CD}$ . 于是有 $$ \begin{aligned} \overrightarrow{AD}\cdot\overrightarrow{AD} & = (\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BD})\cdot(\overrightarrow{AC}+\overrightarrow{CD})\ \left\lvert\overrightarrow{AD}\right\rvert^2 & = \overrightarrow{AB}\cdot\overrightarrow{AC}+\overrightarrow{AB}\cdot\overrightarrow{CD}+\overrightarrow{BD}\cdot\overrightarrow{AC}+\overrightarrow{BD}\cdot\overrightarrow{CD}\ \left\lvert\overrightarrow{AD}\right\rvert^2 & = \left\lvert\overrightarrow{AB}\right\rvert\left\lvert\overrightarrow{AC}\right\rvert\cos A+\left\lvert\overrightarrow{AB}\right\rvert\left\lvert\overrightarrow{CD}\right\rvert\cos B+\left\lvert\overrightarrow{BD}\right\rvert\left\lvert\overrightarrow{AC}\right\rvert\cos C-\left\lvert\overrightarrow{BD}\right\rvert\left\lvert\overrightarrow{CD}\right\rvert\ x^2 & = bc\cos A + \frac{1}{2}ac\cos B + \frac{1}{2}ab\cos C - \frac{1}{4}a^2\ 2x^2 & = 2bc\cos A + ac\cos B + ab\cos C - \frac{1}{2}a^2 ~. \end{aligned} $$ 由余弦定理 $$ \begin{aligned} bc\cos A & = \frac{b2+c2-a^2}{2} ~,\ ac\cos B & = \frac{a2+c2-b^2}{2} ~,\ ab\cos C & = \frac{a2+b2-c^2}{2} ~. \end{aligned} $$ 代入，得 $$ \begin{aligned} 2x^2 & = b2+c2-a2+\frac{1}{2}a2+\frac{1}{2}c2-\frac{1}{2}b2+\frac{1}{2}a2+\frac{1}{2}b2-\frac{1}{2}c2-\frac{1}{2}a2 ~. \end{aligned} $$ 即 $$ \begin{aligned} 2x^2 & = b2+c2-\frac{1}{2}a^2 ~. \end{aligned} $$ 即 $$ \begin{aligned} b2+c2 & = 2x2+\frac{1}{2}a2 ~. \end{aligned} $$ 第 2 种（余弦定理） 在 $\triangle ABD$ 与 $\triangle ABC$ 中，由余弦定理可得 $$ \begin{cases} a2+c2-b^2 = 2ac\cos B & (1)\ \frac{1}{4}a2+c2-x^2 = ac\cos B & (2) \end{cases} $$ $(2)\times 2-(1)$ 可得 $$ \begin{aligned} -\frac{1}{2}a2+c2+b2-2x2 & = 0 ~. \end{aligned} $$ 即 $$ \begin{aligned} b2+c2 & = 2x2+\frac{1}{2}a2 ~. \end{aligned} $$ 在 $\triangle ACD$ 与 $\triangle ABC$ 中，相似的推理可得相同结论 . 第 3 种（作高）
如图，作 $AE\perp BC$ 于 $E$ . 若 $E$ 在 $D$ 的左侧，设 $AE=h,BE=y$，有 $$ \begin{cases} h2+y2=c^2 & (1)\ h2+(\frac{1}{2}a-y)2=x^2 \iff h2-\frac{1}{4}a2-ay+y2=x2 & (2) \ h2+(a-y)2=b^2 \iff h2+a2-2ay+y2=b2 & (3) \end{cases} $$ $(1)+(3)-(2)\times 2$ 得 $$ \begin{aligned} (h2+y2)+(h2+a2-2ay+y2)-2(h2+\frac{1}{4}a2-ay+y2) & = b2+c2-2x^2 ~. \end{aligned} $$ 即 $$ \begin{aligned} -\frac{1}{2}a^2 & = b2+c2-2x^2 ~. \end{aligned} $$ 即 $$ \begin{aligned} b2+c2 & = 2x2+\frac{1}{2}a2 ~. \end{aligned} $$

entry.content:
我们不建议阅读下面的文字。译者仅进行了十分业余的翻译，不对无论是翻译质量还是下面文字所述的内容的正确性或公正性负任何责任。 We do not recommend reading the following text. The translator has merely provided a very amateur translation and assumes no responsibility for the quality of the translation or the accuracy or impartiality of the content below.
Letter to Jiang Qing[1][2] (8th July, 1966) Author: Mao Zedong Jiang Qing[3]: I received your letter of 29th June. It would be best for you to stay there for a while, following the advice of Comrades Wei and Chen[4]. I have two foreign guests to meet this month; shall tell you my whereabouts after meeting them. Since leaving Wulin[5] on 15th June, I have been living in a mountain cave in the west[6] for over ten days, thus being somehow out of touch with the news. I arrived at the land of ‘White Clouds and Yellow Cranes’[7], and have been here for ten days. Reading the materials every day is very interesting all the time. Under heaven, great disorder leads to great order. It happens every seven or eight years. The ‘ox-demons and snake-spirits’ will jump out of their own accord. Driven by their own class natures, they have no choice but to jump out. The Central Committee urges to distribute my friend’s speech[8], and I am preparing for accepting the release—he focused specially on the issue of coups. No one had ever discussed the issue as he did. I have always felt uneasy about some of his formulations. I never believed such magical powers ever exist in those small books of mine. Now, after his touting, the whole Party and the whole nationhave joined in the hype—truly a case of ringing my own bell. I was forced by them onto Mount Liang; it seems that I have to agree with them. It is the first time for me to approve others on such a major issue against my own judgment; such should be called ‘unmovable to humans’ will’. Ruan Ji of Jin Dynasty opposed Liu Bang; walking from Luoyang to Chen’gao, he signed: ‘With no heroes in the world, mere scoundrels made themselves a name.’ Lu Xun said similar things for his miscellaneous essays; I share a kindred mind with Lu Xun. I like his way of being frank. He said: ‘Dissecting oneself is often harder than dissecting others.’ After tumbling several times, I often do that as well. But fellow comrades do not believe it usually; I am confident but also somehow inconfident. When I was young, I once said: ‘Confident that I shall live two hundred years, I will strike the waters over three thousand li.’ That just shows what high spirits I was in. However, I was not so confident, always feeling it will be ‘with no tigers in the mountain, monkeys will claim to be king.’ I just became a king like this. But it was not eclecticism as well; there is some ‘tiger spirits’ on me, prominently; also there is some ‘monkey spirits’, secondarily. I used to cite several sentences from the letter written by Li Gu of Eastern Han Dynasty to Huang Qiong: ‘Yáoyao zhě yì zhé, jiǎojiǎo zhě yì wū. Yángchūn báixuě, hé zhě gài guǎ. Shèngmíng zhī xià, qíshí nán fù.’[9] The latter two sentences just meant me. I once read these sentences at the meeting of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau. Self-knowledge is a virtue. At the Hangzhou Meeting this April, I expressed disagreement with the ways my friends expressed it. But what good did it do? He still talked about it like that at the Beijing Meeting in May; The newspapers and magazines trumpeted it even more fiercely—extolling me in almost supernatural terms. In this way, I have to go onto Mount Liang. I guess their incentives are to use ‘Zhong Kui’ to beat ghosts. I just became the ‘Zhong Kui’ of the Communist Party in the 1960s. Things will always go to the opposite, rising higher, tumbling harder; I am preparing to tumble into pieces. That is nothing at all: matter is indestructible; just into pieces it is. There are more than one hundred Parties in the world, most of them not believing in Marxism-Leninism, and Marx and Lenin themselves have been shattered by people—so what chances do we have? I urge you to pay attention to this problem: do not let victory go to your head, and think about your own weaknesses, shortcomings and faults. I talked this issue with you for countless times; you must remember that I have just talked it in Shanghai in April. The writing above is rather ‘black talk’; don’t some counter-party elements just say it like this? But they intend to overthrow our entire Party and myself, while I merely speak of that some characterisations of my role are inappropriate; that is the difference between me and the ‘black gang.’ This matter cannot be made public; The entire left-wing and broad masses hold this view. If we made it public, we are spraying cold water on them and helping the right-wing; the mission now is to fundamentally (completely is not possible) beat the right-wing down, and a movement to sweep the ‘ox-demons and snake-spirits’ would be done seven or eight years later; there will be more later. Thus these nearly ‘black talks’ of mine must not be made public; when to make it public can not be determined at the moment, because the left-wing and broad masses will not welcome me saying like this. Maybe sometime after my death, when the right-wing hold the power, let them make it public. They will use my talks like this to attempt to raise the ‘black flag’ forever; but if they do that, they will bring about their own downfall. Since the emperor was beaten in 1911, reactionary regimes in China never lasted long, the longest of them lasting a merely twenty years (under Chiang Kai-shek), which falled the moment the people raise the flag for rebellion. Chiang Kai-shek exploited Sun Yat-sen’s trust of him to establish the Whampoa Military School, gathering a bunch of reactionaries forming his power. Once he turned against the Communists, nearly all of the landlords and bourgeoisie classes support him; the Communist Party still lacking experience then, he rose to power happily and temporarily. But in this twenty years, he never achieved true unification: there was the war between the Kuomintang and the CPC, the war between KMT and various warlord factions, the Sino-Japanese War, and finally the four-year great civil war; after that he was driven to a group of islands. If a counter-communist right-wing coup happened in China, I bet they would find no peace and would be short-lived, for all of the revolutionaries representing more than ninety percent of the people’s interests will not tolerate it. At then the right-wing may cite my words to rise in a time, and the left-wing will cite my other words to organise themselves and overthrow them. This Great Cultural Revolution is a serious rehearsal. Some regions (like Beijing City) have there roots deep, and will vanish overnight; some certain institutions have entrenched networks, and will be dissected soon. The more arrogant the right-wing are, the more disastrous their defeat will be, and the more spirited the left-wing will become. This is a national rehearsal, and all the left-wing, the right-wing and the wavering middle-wing will get their own lessons. Conclusion: the future is bright, the road is tortuous—still these two old sayings. The Resolution of Publishing The Selected Works of Mao Zedong and Preparing for the Publication of The Complete Works of Mao Zedong by the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China In more than half a century, the great leader and tutor Chairman Mao Zedong has inherited, defended and developed Marxism-Leninism and has enriched the theoretic treasure-house of Marxism, according to the principles of uniting the universal truths of Marxism-Leninism with the specific practice of revolution, in the great struggle of leading our country to complete the New-Democratic Revolution and carry out the Socialist Revolution and Socialist Construction, in the great struggle of opposing the right-wing and ‘left-wing’ opportunist lines in the Party, and in the great struggle of opposing modern revisionism centred around the Soviet revisionist traitor group and reactionaries in various countries. Publishing the works of Chairman Mao has great realistic significance and far-reaching historical significance both to our country’s people to inherit Chairman Mao’s unfulfilled wish and carry the proletarian revolutionary cause through to the end and to the liberation cause of the world’s proletariats and the oppressed people of oppressed nations. This is a great deed in the developing history of Marxism, and it is a must to carry out the work seriously and diligently with utmost care. The Central Committee of the Communist Party of China has decided that: (Ⅰ) Publish the fifth volume of The Selected Works of Mao Zedong as soon as possible, and successively publish further volumes. While publishing The Selected Works, actively prepare for the publication of The Complete Works of Mao Zedong. (Ⅱ) The publication of The Selected Works of Mao Zedong and The Complete Works of Mao Zedong should be directly led by the Political Bureau of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China headed by Comrade Hua Guofeng. A Committee of Editing and Publishing the Works of Chairman Mao Zedong should be established under the Political Bureau to be responsible for the specific work of sorting, editing and publishing. (Ⅲ) All the original copies of Chairman Mao’s works should be collected and preserved by the General Office of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China. The Central Committee instructs Party Committees at all levels to promptly submit all of Chairman Mao’s manuscripts preserved in their respective regions and units, including original copies of articles, files, telegrams, instructions, letters, poems, inscriptions, and original transcriptions of speeches, to the General Office of the Central Committee. The Central Committee of the Communist Party of China calls upon the entire Party, the entire Army, and the people of all nationalities throughout the country to launch a new upsurge in studying Marxist-Leninist works and Chairman Mao’s works, and to vigorously assist in collecting original copies of Chairman Mao’s works. The Central Committee of the Communist Party of China hopes that Marxist-Leninist political parties, organisations, progressive groups, and friendly individuals from all countries will assist in the collection of original copies of Chairman Mao’s works.
The Central Committee of the Communist Party of China 8th October, 1976
Publisher’s Note to the Fifth Volume of The Selected Works of Mao Zedong The works of the great leader and tutor, Chairman Mao Zedong, are immortal contributions to Marxism-Leninism. In the light of the resolution of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China, the fifth volume of The Selected Works of Mao Zedong is now published; further volumes will also be published in succession. The first to the fourth volumes of The Selected Works of Mao Zedong published in the past are important works during the New-Democratic Revolution period. The fifth and further volumes are important works during the Socialist Revolution and Socialist Construction period. In the new historical period after the founding of the People’s Republic of China, Comrade Mao Zedong persisted in the consistent principles of uniting the universal truths of Marxism-Leninism with the specific practice of revolution, and led our Party and the people of our country inherit, defend and developed Marxism-Leninism in the struggle of carrying out the Socialist Revolution and Socialist Construction, in the struggle of opposing the revisionist lines of Gao-Rao, Peng Dehuai, Liu Shaoqi, Lin Biao, and Wang-Zhang-Jiang-Yao, in the struggle of opposing imperialism and reactionaries in various countries, and in the struggle of opposing modern revisionism centred around the Soviet revisionist traitor group. In this period, the greatest theoretic contributions of Comrade Mao Zedong is that he systematically summarised the historical experiences of the proletarian dictatorship both international and of our country, applied the basic standpoint of the unity of opposites of materialist dialectics, analysed the laws of development of socialism, and established the great theory of Continuing Revolution Under Proletarian Dictatorship. The new thought and theory of proletarian revolution and proletarian dictatorship by Comrade Mao Zedong, greatly enriched the theoretic treasure-house of Marxism-Leninism in the fields of philosophy, political economy and scientific socialism. It not only points out the fundamental road to consolidating proletarian dictatorship, guarding against restoration of capitalism, and constructing socialism, but possesses great, far-reaching global significance as well. The fifth volume of The Selected Works of Mao Zedong contains important works from July 1949 to 1957. The scientific thesis of conflicts between the proletariat and the bourgeoisie and between the socialist road and the capitalist road still long-lastingly exist after the basic accomplishment of the socialist transformation of the system of ownership of the means of production, the theory of how to distinguish and deal with the two contradictions of different nature, contradictions between ourselves and the enemy and contradictions among the people, correctly, the great theory of Continuing Revolution Under Proletarian Dictatorship, and the basic concept of the general line of socialist construction by Comrade Mao Zedong are first advanced in this volume of works, Later, especially in the Great Proletarian Cultural Revolution, Comrade Mao Zedong continually enriched and developed these glorious thoughts according to the experiences of revolutional practice. Comrade Mao Zedong was the greatest Marxist-Leninist in the contemporary era. Mao Zedong Thought is the victorious flag of the unitedly fighting and continuing revolution of our Party, our Army, and our people, and is the common treasure of international proletariats and each country’s revolutionary people. The thoughts and theories of Comrade Mao Zedong are immortal. The selected works of Comrade Mao Zedong during the period of the Socialist Revolution and Socialist Construction have part of them publicly issued in the past, the others not, including the files, manuscripts and speeches’ formal transcripts by Comrade Mao Zedong. Speech transcripts were essentially, technically straightened out when editing.
The Committee of Editing and Publishing the Works of Chairman Mao Zedong of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China 1st March, 1977

entry.title: Weird Translations
entry.content:
Thought at Quiet Night Author: LI Bai [Tang Dynasty] Bed front bright moon light, Be frost on ground it might. Head up to watch bright moon, Head down it’s nostalgia I knew.
静夜思 李白【唐】 床前明月光，疑是地上霜。 举头望明月，低头思故乡。
Watching the Sea Tides (DONGNANXINGSHENG) Author: LIU Yong [Northern Song Dynasty] Attractions in the southeast, capital of the triple Wu, since ancient times is Qiantang so prosperous. Smoky willows, gorgeous bridges, window-covering windows and turquoise screen, leads to the hundred thousands of families. Tall trees that grow into the clouds surround the dam sands; angry waves wrap the snow-like sprays; the natural chasm is boundless. Jewelry displayed at markets, satin filled in houses; people compete in extravagance. Duplicated lakes and overlapped ranges are beautiful; there are laurels in autumn and ten miles of lotus flowers in summer. Qiang pipes trick sunny days, fishermen’s songs spread the night, joyful are the fishing old men and the lotus children. Thousand riders surround the High Tooth, by drunk listen to the xiao and drums, appreciate the smoky colourful clouds alone. Other day draw this great scenery, back to the Phoenix Pool praise.
望海潮（东南形胜） 柳永【北宋】 东南形胜，三吴都会，钱塘自古繁华。烟柳画桥，风帘翠幕，参差十万人家。云树绕堤沙，怒涛卷霜雪，天堑无涯。市列珠玑，户盈罗绮，竞豪奢。 重湖叠𪩘清嘉，有三秋桂子，十里荷花。羌管弄晴，菱歌泛夜，嬉嬉钓叟莲娃。千骑拥高牙，乘醉听萧鼓，吟赏烟霞。异日图将好景，归去凤池夸。
Sichuan Road is Difficult Author: LI Bai [Tang Dynasty] Ah ah ah, so dangerous, so high! The difficulty of Sichuan Road, is more to climbing up the blue sky! Kings Cancong and Yufu, how obscure was their kingdom founded! From then forty-eight thousand years, none with Qin stronghold through human smoke. West to Mount Taibai are bird paths, which are able to fly over peak of Mount Emei. Grounds broke, mountains collapsed, robust men died, then sky ladders and stone stacks were linked. Up are high tops that make the sun’s six loongs return, down are torrents swirling caused by rapid streams refluxing when crushing rocks. High flights by yellow swans cannot yet pass, apes hesitate climbing when trying to get through. Mount Qingni is so hooling twisty, hundred steps with nine turns go round its peaks. Touch Star Shen, pass Star Jing, look up and hold your breath; put hands on chest, sit and sigh deeply. I ask you: when to return from your westward journey? Scary ways and precipitous rocks cannot be climbed; only to see sorrowful bird crying for ancient woods, males flying and females chasing round the trees, and to listen to cuckoos singing night moons, and worrying empty mountains. Harder than climbing up the blue sky is the Sichuan Road, people who hear this, their rosy cheeks will die away! Continuously linked-up crests are less than one foot from the sky; withered pines hang upside-down on cliffs. Flying torrents and waterfall flows compete for noise, crashing the cliffs, pushing the rocks, thunder roaring between ridges. How dangerous it is, you afar for what to come? Jian’ge is so high and towering, that one man in defence can reject hundreds of thousands of men. If untrustworthy men defend it, they will turn into wolves and jackals. Early avoid fierce tigers, late avoid long snakes, grind teeth, suck blood, kill men like hemp. Silk city is though said happy, you’d better get home early. Sichuan Road is so difficult, turn and look west, sigh long.
蜀道难 李白【唐】 噫吁嚱，危乎高哉！蜀道之难，难于上青天！蚕丛及鱼凫，开国何茫然！尔来四万八千岁，不与秦塞通人烟。西当太白有鸟道，可以横绝峨眉巅。地崩山摧壮士死，然后天梯石栈相钩连。上有六龙回日之高标，下有冲波逆折之回川。黄鹤之飞尚不得过，猿猱欲度愁攀援。青泥何盘盘，百步九折萦岩峦。扪参历井仰胁息，以手抚膺坐长叹。 问君西游何时还？畏途巉岩不可攀。但见悲鸟号古木，雄飞雌从绕林间。又闻子规啼夜月，愁空山。蜀道之难，难于上青天，使人听此凋朱颜！连峰去天不盈尺，枯松倒挂倚绝壁。飞湍瀑流争喧豗，砯崖转石万壑雷。其险也如此，嗟尔远道之人胡为乎来哉！ 剑阁峥嵘而崔嵬，一夫当关，万夫莫开。所守或匪亲，化为狼与豺。朝避猛虎，夕避长蛇，磨牙吮血，杀人如麻。锦城虽云乐，不如早还家。蜀道之难，难于上青天，侧身西望长咨嗟！
The Barbaric Bodhisattva (XIAOSHANCHONGDIEJINMINGMIE) Author: WEN Tingyun [Tang Dynasty] Small hills overlapping and gold glimmering, cloud-like hair seeming to drift over the snowing fragrant cheek. Lazily got up to draw the moth-like brows; it was late to wash and do make-up. Checking the flower from the double mirrors, in which the face and flowers shone upon each other. Newly embroidered Ruqun on, with pairs of golden partridges.
菩萨蛮（小山重叠金明灭） 温庭筠【唐】 小山重叠金明灭，鬓云欲度香腮雪。懒起画蛾眉，弄妆梳洗迟。照花前后镜，花面交相映。新贴绣罗襦，双双金鹧鸪。
Green Curtain Covers (LIAOCHENXIANG) Author: ZHOU Bangyan [Northern Song Dynasty] Burnt the eaglewood, to erase summer’s moisty heat. Birds hailing the sunlight, at dawn chirping while peeking at the eave. Early sun dried the night’s rain on leaves; on the clear and round water, every water lily stood out in the morning wind. So far is my hometown, then on which day would I ever set off? Near Wu my family lives, but so long have I been a traveller in Chang’an. Remember or not the fishing lad in May? With small paddles on a light boat, I dreamt into a lotus pond.
苏幕遮（燎沉香） 周邦彦【北宋】 燎沉香，消溽暑。鸟雀呼晴，侵晓窥檐语。叶上初阳干宿雨，水面清圆，一一风荷举。 故乡遥，何日去？家住吴门，久作长安旅。五月渔郎相忆否？小楫轻舟，梦入芙蓉浦。
The Barbaric Bodhisattva : Written on the Zaokou Wall in Jiangxi Author: XIN Qiji [Southern Song Dynasty] Clear river flows below the Yugu Tower, inside dissolved how many refugees’ tears! Gazing afar to the northwest for Chang’an, such a pity so many mountains lie between. Green mountains can’t block the way; water flows to the east after all. 'Night near the river I was worrying, when partridge sounds entered my ears from the deep mountain.
菩萨蛮·书江西造口壁 辛弃疾【南宋】 郁孤台下清江水，中间多少行人泪。西北望长安，可怜无数山。 青山遮不住，毕竟东流去。江晚正愁余，山深闻鹧鸪。
Turquoise Jade Bowl : The Lantern Festival Author: XIN Qiji [Southern Song Dynasty] 'Night, wind from the east bloomed flowers on thousands of trees. Then blew them off, stars dropped like rain. Fine horses and carved carriages spread out with roads full of scent. Music flew, the moon shone; it was a night of fish and loongs dancing. Moth ornaments, snow-willows, threads of gold; they left with faint fragrances, talking and laughing. Having looked for her hundreds of thousands of times, I suddenly turned round; she was just there, where the light was waning.
青玉案·元夕 辛弃疾【南宋】 东风夜放花千树。更吹落，星如雨。宝马雕车香满路。凤箫声动，玉壶光转，一夜鱼龙舞。 蛾儿雪柳黄金缕，笑语盈盈暗香去。众里寻他千百度，蓦然回首，那人却在，灯火阑珊处。
Reply Letter to REN An (Excerpt) Author: SIMA Qian [Western Han Dynasty] Those people in ancient times that were noble and rich but faded out in history cannot be counted; only the most extraordinary ones are still praised today. King Wen of Zhou was confined and then deduced The Book of Changes; Confucius suffered adversity and The Spring and Autumn Annals was written; QU Yuan was exiled so he wrote the poem Lisao; ZUO Qiuming became blind and The Discourses of the States thus emerged; SUN Bin’s kneecaps were chopped, and then he composed his Art of War; LÜ Buwei was demoted to Sichuan, and then Lüshi Chunqiu passed on to generations; HAN Fei was imprisoned in Qin and then there came out Shuonan and Gufen; the three hundred poems of The Book of Songs were mostly written by wise people venting their grievances. These people all have stressful and upset feelings and cannot realise their ideals, so they wrote about past deeds, hoping that people would read them in the future. Just like ZUO Qiuming having his eyes blind, SUN Bin having his leg broken; they cannot be put to significant use for the rest of their lives, so they stepped back, wrote books and established theories to let out their bad feelings, wanting to leave writings presenting their own thoughts. I privately put a quart into a pint pot, and have recently used those low-level words of mine, to collect the missing historic deeds, roughly examine their truths, summarise their ins and outs, and inspect the laws of how they succeed, fail, rise, or fall; from the Yellow Emperor to the current era, I have written ten Tables, twelve Benji, eight Books, thirty Shijia, seventy Liezhuan, in total one hundred and thirty pieces. Also I want to research the relationship between natural phenomena and the human society, have a good command of the threads of the changes from ancient to present, and form a distinctive view. Just having begun and not yet finished, I unfortunately suffered this disaster; I pity that the book can’t be finished, and thus accepted the most cruel punishments without daring be annoyed. Now I have finally finished this book, planning to hide it into famous mountains, pass on to people worthy of it, and let it spread in big cities; then, I have compensated for the debt I owed by being disgraced; how can I ever regret even if I were to suffer ten thousand times of that humiliation! However these words can only be spoken to the wise; it is very hard to let the vulgar understand.
报任安书（节选） 司马迁【西汉】 古者富贵而名摩灭，不可胜记，唯倜傥非常之人称焉。盖文王拘而演《周易》；仲尼厄而作《春秋》；屈原放逐，乃赋《离骚》；左丘失明，厥有《国语》；孙子膑脚，《兵法》修列；不韦迁蜀，世传《吕览》；韩非囚秦，《说难》《孤愤》；《诗》三百篇，大底圣贤发愤之所为作也。此人皆意有所郁结，不得通其道，故述往事、思来者。乃如左丘无目，孙子断足，终不可用，退而论书策，以舒其愤，思垂空文以自见。 仆窃不逊，近自托于无能之辞，网罗天下放失旧闻，略考其行事，综其终始，稽其成败兴坏之纪，上计轩辕，下至于兹，为十表，本纪十二，书八章，世家三十，列传七十，凡百三十篇。亦欲以究天人之际，通古今之变，成一家之言。草创未就，会遭此祸，惜其不成，是以就极刑而无愠色。仆诚以著此书，藏之名山，传之其人，通邑大都，则仆偿前辱之责，虽万被戮，岂有悔哉！然此可为智者道，难为俗人言也。
Visiting the Son of Heaven : Ode to the Suona Horn Author: WANG Pan [Ming Dynasty] Trumpets, suona horns, tunes small but sounds loud. Official boats come and go messily like hemp, all depending on you to raise their status. On hearing you armies become anxious, civilians become frightened. Where to find whether it is real or fake? See it blow overturn this family, blow hurt that family; just blow until water exhaust and geese fly!
朝天子·咏喇叭 王磐【明】 喇叭，唢呐，曲儿小腔儿大。官船来往乱如麻，全仗你抬声价。军听了军愁，民听了民怕。哪里去辨甚么真共假？眼见的吹翻了这家，吹伤了那家，只吹的水尽鹅飞罢！
The Book of Rites : Conveyance of Rites (Excerpt) When the Great Way prevailed, the whole world is as one community. People select the virtuous, vote the talented, speak of honesty and build harmony. Then people do not only treat relatives as relatives, do not only treat their children as their children, and ensure that the old have their ends, the strong have their use, the young have their growth; widowers, widows, orphans, the childless and the disabled are all supported; the male have their limits, and the female have their families. Things, one hates them being thrown onto the ground, not wanting to keep it oneself; Force, one hates it not coming from one’s own, not wanting interest for oneself. Like this, schemes vanish and never rise; theft and raid are never done; thus outward doors never close. This is what is called the ‘Great Unity’.
礼记·礼运（节选） 大道之行也，天下为公。选贤与能，讲信修睦。故人不独亲其亲，不独子其子，使老有所终，壮有所用，幼有所长，矜、寡、孤、独废疾者皆有所养，男有分，女有归。货恶其弃于地也，不必藏于己；力恶其不出于身也，不必为己。是故谋闭而不兴，盗窃乱贼而不作，故外户而不闭。是谓大同。

entry.title: OI 名言
entry.content:
《OI 子》三章
《骗分榜一，暴力爆零》by 20210732ktq 正解不如暴力，暴力不如骗分。一道题目，两种做法，想而编之而WA。夫想而编之，必有得正解者矣，然而WA者，是正解不如暴力也。手非不酸也，码非不短也，部分分非不多也，暴力非不正确也，排名第二，是暴力不如骗分也。故曰，AC不以思路之深，暴力不以代码之短，首杀不以手速之快。骗分者榜一，暴力者爆零。爆零之至，老师骂之。榜一之至，全球膜之。以全球之所膜，攻教练之所骂，故OIer有不战，战必AK。
《水题不能淫》by 20210927chr chr曰：“ktq，xcx岂不诚奆佬哉？骗分而OIers惧，正解而OI熄。” xrz曰：“是焉得为奆佬乎？子未学OI乎？奆佬之冠也，zc命之，蒟蒻之冠也，ls命之，往送之CSP，戒之曰：‘往之CSP，必敬必戒，无违考规！’以骗为正者，蒟蒻之道也。做天下之难题，写天下之正解，AK天下之比赛。AK，与OIers由之；不AK，自己切题。水题不能淫，难题不能移，毒瘤不能屈，此之谓奆佬。”

entry.title: 《又四日文集》序
entry.content:
欣闻又四日先生（AllInTime）决定编辑这部《又四日文集》，又命不才任主编一职，不胜感激，故为又四日先生作序一篇，谨此。 余初识又四日先生，已是公元纪年二〇二三年矣。自昔日起，便发现又四日先生素有非凡不同于常人之气质也。又四日先生虽形容枯槁，体形瘦削，但见过他的人必会发现他神情严肃，姿态挺拔，颇有一代豪杰之势也。与他交往数日，闻者必得深刻之见解，因是又四日先生常用独到而一针见血的推理，得出深刻而精致的结论，并用他那朴实、简洁而又精确的浅显语言表达出口，传至听者之耳，使其顿悟得人生大道；然再细细咀嚼，又可品出其背后又四日先生的独家精髓。 余阅又四日先生之文，实乃近二年之事也，未敢详细评之。但阅前余便认定，又四日先生之文章，必是与其实人相似风格之物矣。阅，确如此。俗语言曰：“字如其人，文亦如其人。”又四日先生之字迹，实与其本人一致，粗犷而豪放；虽潦草但不失风度，虽崎岖却不丢端正。读又四日先生之字，恰似研究那古体文字，优美而透有庄重、沉稳之感。再详读又四日先生之数十篇文章，可见又四日先生之见识广博，语言深入而不失瑰丽之感。无论是像“社会性的严肃可得严肃性的社会”这样的对社会的剖析，还是像“湖中岛，岛中湖。人中心，心中人”这样的对人情感的深挖，都凸显出又四日先生独特的处世哲学。 先生“又四日”之名号，实为拆字之法。而得“又四日”三字，又正符先生之性情特征，故先生取之以作号也。“又四日”者，四日一计，方有其“四”；而生命无穷，故有“又”字居于词头。“又四日”云云，实蕴生命之无穷，而又循环周始也。 呜呼！世如又四日先生之人，有几何哉？幸今有此《又四日文集》存，而先生之言得以永传焉。
AppOfficer 二〇二六年二月一日夜，子时
